summary: The chord construction and the argument under positive line mass are coherent, but the stated final consequence is false in the zero-mass boundary case.
critical_errors: Condition (7) does not imply L_ell>0 when W=0, although the proof later asserts "Since L_ell>0" and uses (6), which was proved only under that hypothesis. For a concrete counterexample, take d=1 and let C be the closed Euclidean ball of radius 1/4 centered at ((1/2,1/2),0) in R^2 x R. Its base projection contains no point of Z^2, so W=0 and C intersected with (Z^2 x R) is empty. With u=(1,0) and ell=R x {0}, one has L_ell=0, hence (7) holds as 0>=0, but there is no mixed-lattice point at all, contradicting the claimed consequence.
repair_hints: State the final consequence under the standing hypothesis L_ell>0, or assume W>0; then (7) forces L_ell>0 and permits the use of (6).
